subject: History
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentence: It may be said that ______ was the founder of modern historiography.
solution: **(A)** Voltaire. It may be said that Voltaire was the founder of modern historiography. Voltaire (1694-1778), whose original name was François-Marie Arouet, was French. He held that along with objective truth and the chronology of historical events, social traditions, trade, economy, agriculture and similar aspects were equally important in historiography. This gave rise to the thought that understanding all aspects of human life is important for history writing, and so he is called the founder of modern historiography.

subject: History
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentence: The ______ saw the rise of Mathura school.
solution: **(A)** Kushana period. The Kushana period saw the rise of Mathura school. The 1st-3rd century C.E., that is the Kushana period, saw the rise of the Mathura school of art, and this school laid the foundation of Indian iconography. The Kushana kings also used images of various deities on their coins. The iconographic rules and standards for sculptural art were formulated later, in the period of the Gupta empire.

subject: History
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the sentence: ______ at Kolkata is the first museum in India.
solution: **(D)** Indian Museum. The Indian Museum at Kolkata is the first museum in India. It was established by the Asiatic Society of Bengal in Kolkata in 1814 C.E. The second museum in India, the Government Museum, was established in Chennai in 1851 C.E., while the National Museum is in Delhi and the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastusangrahalay is in Mumbai.

subject: History
stem: Identify the wrong pair in the following and write: (i) Rene Descartes - 'Discourse on the Method'; (ii) Karl Marx - 'Das Capital'; (iii) Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel - 'Reason in History'; (iv) Leopold von Ranke - 'The Histories'.

options.label: C
options.text: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel - 'Reason in History'

solution: **(D)** Leopold von Ranke - 'The Histories'. This pair is wrong. 'The Histories' was written by Herodotus, the Greek historian of the fifth century B.C.E., who was the first to use the term 'History' for his book. The collections of Leopold von Ranke's articles are published in two books, 'The Theory and Practice of History' and 'The Secret of World History'. The other three pairs are correct: Descartes wrote 'Discourse on the Method', Karl Marx wrote 'Das Kapital', and Hegel's book 'Reason in History' is well known.

subject: History
stem: Identify the wrong pair in the following and write: (i) Matheran - Hill Station; (ii) Todoba - Rock-cut Caves; (iii) Kolhapur - Pilgrim Centre; (iv) Ajanta - World Heritage.
solution: **(B)** Todoba - Rock-cut Caves. This pair is wrong. Tadoba is a sanctuary, one of the important tourist centres of Maharashtra along with the sanctuaries at Dajipur and Sagareshwar; it is not a site of rock-cut caves. The famous rock-cut caves of Maharashtra are at Ajanta, Verul and Gharapuri (Elephanta). The other three pairs are correct: Matheran is a hill station, Kolhapur is a pilgrim centre, and the Ajanta caves were declared World Heritage in 1983.

subject: History
stem: Identify the wrong pair in the following and write: (i) Mallakhamb - Outdoor game based on physical skills; (ii) Water Polo - Water sport; (iii) Skating - Adventurous ice sport; (iv) Chess - Outdoor game.

options.label: A
options.text: Mallakhamb - Outdoor game based on physical skills

solution: **(D)** Chess - Outdoor game. This pair is wrong. Chess is an indoor game. Indoor games are played within a closed environment and many of them are played sitting at one place, such as chess, card games and carom. The other three pairs are correct: mallakhamb is an outdoor sport based on physical skills, water polo is a water sport, and ice skating is an adventurous game that requires balancing skills.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on: Art.
solution: It is a natural human instinct to want to share one's experience, wisdom and emotions. When that instinct results in a beautiful creation, it is acknowledged as 'Art'. The artist's power of imagination, sensibility, state of emotion and skills are the crucial factors at the root of artistic creation. Artistic creations are of two types: visual arts (Drik Kala), such as painting and sculpture, and performing arts (Lalit or Aangik Kala). The prehistoric rock art discovered at many sites in the world proves that visual arts are as old as the stone-age man. There are two distinct traditions of art: folk art, which is a spontaneous part of people's way of living and is created by the collective participation of a social group, and classical art, which follows an established frame of rules and needs prolonged training. When a style is adopted by many artists over a long time it becomes an 'art style', and such styles help us study art history.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on: The role of newspaper in the Indian struggle for independence.
solution: Printing technology and newspapers came to India after the arrival of the British, and newspapers became the first mass medium of circulating information and knowledge among people. In the pre-independence period newspapers were a very important medium of creating social awareness. 'Darpan', started in 1832 in Mumbai by Balshastri Jambhekar, reported political, economic, social and cultural events. 'Prabhakar' of Bhau Mahajan published Lokhitvadi's 'Shatpatre' to create social awareness, 'Induprakash' supported widow remarriage, and 'Deenbandhu' of Krishnarao Bhalekar spoke for the masses. 'Kesari' and 'Maratha', started in 1881 by Gopal Ganesh Agarkar and Bal Gangadhar Tilak, discussed the social and political issues of the period and published articles about the nationwide situation and the politics in England. Thus newspapers carried news to the people and created social and political awareness among them, and as historical documents that record current events they are also an important source for the history of the freedom struggle.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on: Dictionaries.
solution: Dictionaries are one of the four types of encyclopaedia, the others being the comprehensive encyclopaedia (Vishwakosh), encyclopaedic (Koshsadrush) literature and indexes. A dictionary arranges the words of a language in a certain order, most commonly the alphabetical order, and gives their meanings, synonyms and etymology. There are various types of dictionaries: comprehensive dictionaries, dictionaries which include only a certain type of words, dictionaries of terminology dealing with the terms peculiar to a branch of knowledge, etymological dictionaries, thesauruses, and dictionaries of idioms and proverbs. India has an ancient tradition of dictionaries such as 'Nighantu' and 'Shabdakosh'. Dictionaries help readers and researchers understand words correctly and preserve the knowledge of a language.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons: Bakhar is an important type of historical documents.
solution: A bakhar is a historical document of medieval times. It contains eulogies of heroes and stories of historic events, battles and the lives of great men, so it gives us information about the events and people of that period. Bakhars are of various types, such as biographies of kings, dynastic histories, descriptions of events, histories of a sect and autobiographies. For example, the 'Sabhasad Bakhar', written by Krishnaji Anant Sabhasad during the reign of Chhatrapati Rajaram Maharaj, is important for information about the rule of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the 'Bhausahebanchi Bakhar' describes the Battle of Panipat, and the 'Holkaranchi Kaiphiyat' gives information about the Holkars. Hence bakhar is an important type of historical documents.

subject: History
subtopic: Applied History and Research in Various Fields
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons: It is essential to study the history of technology.
solution: The history of technology helps us understand the changes, and their causes, in agricultural production, commodity production, architecture, engineering and similar fields. Scientific discoveries and technological advancement depend on each other, and knowledge of science and technology was very important at every step of human evolution, from the making of stone tools to agricultural production. Later the advancement of science promoted the mechanisation of production. To understand how mechanisation developed and how science and technology depend on each other, it is essential to study the history of technology.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons: Knowledge of History is essential for newspaper articles.
solution: Newspapers have to give fresh news, and they must also unfold the background of an event. For this reporters compare it with parallel events of the past, and newspapers run columns such as '50 Years Ago' or '100 Years Ago' that are based on historical documents. On important anniversaries, such as the 100th year of World War I in 2014 or 75 years of the 'Quit India' movement in 2017, newspapers publish supplements, special issues, articles, editorials and reviews, which require a review of the history of the event. Therefore knowledge of history is essential for writing newspaper articles.

subject: History
subtopic: Sources of History, their Conservation and Preservation
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons: Only trained persons, who are duly qualified can take up the tasks involved in the work of conservation and preservation.
solution: Every step in this work, such as collecting the sources of history, preparing their records and indexes, and exhibiting manuscripts, old books and artefacts after the necessary treatments, needs very careful handling and management. The work needs specific skills: knowledge of scripts like Brahmi, Modi and Persian, of the types of paper, ink and colours, of the properties of stones and metals, of archaeological method, and of the equipment and chemicals used for cleaning and conservation. A wrong treatment can permanently damage a document or an artefact, which cannot be replaced. Therefore only trained persons who are duly qualified can take up the tasks of conservation and preservation.

Temples in Maharashtra built in 12th-13th centuries are known as Hemadpanti temples. The outer walls of Hemadpanti temples are built in a star shape. In the star-shaped plan, the outer walls of the temple has a zigzag design. This results into an interesting effect of alternating light and shadow. The important characteristic of Hemadpanti temple is its masonry. The walls are built without using any mortar, by locking the stones by using the technique of tenon and mortise joints. The Ambreshwar temple at Ambarnath near Mumbai, Gondeshwar temple at Sinnar near Nashik, Aundha Nagnath temple in the Hingoli district are a few finest examples of the Hemadpanti style. Their plan is star-shaped. The Hemadpanti temples are found at several places in Maharashtra.
stem: How are the outer walls of Hemadpanti temples built?
solution: The outer walls of Hemadpanti temples are built in a star shape, with a zigzag design.

stem: What are the main characteristics of Hemadpanti temples?
solution: The main characteristics of Hemadpanti temples are: (1) They were built in Maharashtra in the 12th-13th centuries and their plan is star-shaped. (2) The outer walls have a zigzag design, which creates an interesting effect of alternating light and shadow. (3) Their most important characteristic is the masonry: the walls are built without any mortar, by locking the stones with the technique of tenon and mortise joints.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail: Explain Karl Marx's class theory.
solution: Karl Marx (1818-1883) put forward a new thesis in the latter half of the nineteenth century, which gave rise to a new school of thought. His class theory can be explained as follows: (1) According to Marx, history is not about abstract ideas; it is about living people. (2) Human relationships are shaped by the fundamental needs of people and by the ownership as well as the nature of the means of production available to meet those needs. (3) The accessibility of these means of production to the different strata of society is not equal. (4) This inequality divides society into classes, which leads to class struggle. (5) The class that owns the means of production economically exploits the rest of the classes, and so, according to Marx, human history is the history of class struggle. His treatise 'Das Kapital' is the most referred book all over the world.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail: How can we correlate Applied History with our present?
solution: People often ask about the practical value of history, and applied history answers this question. (1) The visible and invisible relics of the past exist in the present, and we feel curiosity and attraction towards them. (2) They represent the creative thoughts and traditions of our ancestors. They are our heritage and help in building our identity, and the history of our heritage links us with our origin. (3) Hence it becomes necessary to preserve and conserve this heritage for our own benefit and for future generations. Applied history is concerned with the preservation and conservation of our heritage and with making it accessible to people. (4) Heritage management also creates opportunities of employment. (5) Knowledge of history provides guidance in finding solutions to contemporary social issues and in social planning. In brief, applied history means understanding our present with the help of history and finding the right direction for the benefit of our future.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail: Explain the close tie between Sports and History.
solution: Although sports and history appear to be distant as subjects, there is a close tie between them. (1) To play is a natural human instinct, so the history of sports begins with the origin of mankind. Ancient Indian literature and epics mention games such as dice, wrestling, horse and chariot races and chess, and the ancient Olympic competitions were held at Olympia in Greece. (2) Toys and game materials found in excavations throw light on history, technological development and cultural contacts; an ivory doll made by Indian craftsmen found at Pompeii throws light on Indo-Roman trade. (3) Sports journalism needs history: articles and reviews about events like the Olympics or the Asiad require historical knowledge. (4) An expert commentator needs good knowledge of the history, statistics, previous records, eminent players and anecdotes of the game, as Bal J. Pandit showed in his cricket commentaries. (5) Making movies on sports and on the biographies of players, such as 'Mary Kom' and 'Dangal', requires a deep study of the period, and books and encyclopaedias of sports, such as the history of Mallakhamb, are being written. Thus history and sports are closely connected.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail: Why is Maharashtra known as the land that nurtured the Indian Film Industry? Explain with examples.
solution: The honour of making and releasing the first full length movie goes to Maharashtra, and so Maharashtra is known as the land that nurtured the Indian film industry. (1) Dadasaheb Torane (Gopal Ramchandra Torane), with A. P. Karandikar, S. N. Patankar and V. P. Divekar, made the movie 'Pundalik' with the help of foreign technicians; it was released in Mumbai in 1912. (2) 'Raja Harishchandra', directed by Dadasaheb Phalke, was the first movie processed completely in India and was released in Mumbai in 1913. Phalke also made 'Mohini-Bhasmasur' and 'Savitri-Satyavana'. (3) Anandrao Painter made the first cine-camera of Indian make, and Baburao Painter made 'Sairandhri' in 1918 and the first historical movie 'Simhgarh', besides 'Savakari Pash' on a social issue. (4) Bhalaji Pendharkar made 'Bajirao-Mastani' in 1925, Kamalabai Mangarulkar became the first woman producer, and the movie 'Sant Tukaram' received international acclaim when it was shown at the international film festival in Paris. (5) Madanrao Madhavrao Pitale, the Patwardhan family of Kalyan and Harishchandra Sakharam Bhatvadekar (Savedada) also contributed to the development of Indian movies.

subject: Political Science
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the statement: The Election Commissioner is appointed by the ______.
solution: **(A)** President. The Election Commissioner is appointed by the President. The Chief Election Commissioner cannot be removed from his post easily or on account of any political reasons, which preserves the independence of the Election Commission.

subject: Political Science
stem: Choose the correct option from the given options and complete the statement: To increase agricultural production and become self-sufficient with regard to food grains ______ was initiated.
solution: **(B)** Green revolution. To increase agricultural production and become self-sufficient with regard to food grains, the Green revolution was initiated. After the Green Revolution the farmers' movement in India became more active and effective.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false and give reasons for your answer: The nature of Constitution is seen as a living document.
solution: True. The Constitution is dynamic. It has to change according to changing conditions, and the Parliament has the power to make those changes. The Judiciary has accepted this power of the Parliament, but has laid down that while amending the Constitution the Parliament cannot alter its basic structure. Because the Constitution keeps changing with the times while keeping its basic framework, it is seen as a living document.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false and give reasons for your answer: The Election Commission lays down the code of conduct during elections.
solution: True. To ensure free and fair elections in India, the Election Commission has adopted several measures, and the Code of Conduct is one of them. It explains the rules that are to be followed by the Government, political parties and voters before and during elections, and even the Government cannot violate these rules. Due to the strict observance of the code of conduct in the last few elections, common voters have become confident.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false and give reasons for your answer: Movements do not need a strong leadership.
solution: False. A movement is a collective action with a particular social objective, and it needs leadership. Leadership keeps the movement active. The objectives of the movement, its programme of action and its strategy of agitation are decided by its leaders. A strong leadership makes the movement effective, so movements do need a strong leadership.

subject: Political Science
stem: Explain the following concept: Policy of reservation of seats.
solution: The policy of reservation of seats is meant for those sections of society who have been deprived of opportunities for education and employment for a long period of time. Accordingly, some seats in educational institutions and in government services are kept reserved for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and there is also a provision of reservation for Other Backward Classes. Seats are also reserved for women and weaker sections in the political process so that they get a share in political power. This policy is an effort of the government to establish social justice and equality and to bring all sections of society into the mainstream.

subject: Political Science
stem: Explain the following concept: Regional parties.
solution: Regional parties are those groups in a region who have a proud feeling about the distinct identity of their region and who compete for political power with the objective of regional development. Their influence is limited to a particular region, but they influence national politics as well. They give preference to the resolution of regional problems and demand more autonomy for the development of the region; they also demand that political power should be in the hands of the people of the region and that its residents should get preference in administration and jobs. Shiv Sena, Telugu Desam, the Shiromani Akali Dal and the Assam Gan Parishad are examples. To be recognised as a regional party, a party has to fulfil the conditions laid down by the Election Commission.

subject: Political Science
stem: Answer in brief: What are the effects of reducing the voting age from 21 years to 18 years?
solution: The Indian Constitution first gave the right to vote equally to men and women above the age of 21 years; the voting age was later reduced from 21 to 18. Its effects are: (1) It gave the young generation in India the opportunity of political participation. (2) India came to have the largest number of voters among democratic nations and became the largest democracy in the world. (3) The change was qualitative as well as quantitative, because new political parties emerged with the active support of young voters, representing the various expectations of people and competing in the political sphere.

subject: Political Science
stem: Answer in brief: What are the effects of criminalisation of politics?
solution: Criminalisation of politics means the increased participation in politics of people with a criminal background, when political parties give candidature to persons facing criminal allegations and allegations of corruption. Its effects are: (1) It increases the role of money and muscle power in politics. (2) It may lead to violence during elections. (3) The Election Commission faces problems in ensuring that elections are conducted in a free environment. To prevent it, the judiciary has adopted measures like strict punishment to criminals and prohibiting criminals from participating in the political process.
